records.question: For an HTTP/2 POST that carries request headers and content, what frame sequence and END flags does RFC 9113 specify?
records.reason: Both responses incorrectly state END_STREAM is set on HEADERS/CONTINUATION frames, when it should only be set on the final DATA frame; neither mentions DATA frames at all, making both incomplete and inaccurate.
records.a_answer: For an HTTP/2 POST that carries request headers and content, the frame sequence consists of a HEADERS frame followed by zero or more CONTINUATION frames containing the serialized block of request header fields. The HEADERS frame has the END_STREAM flag set to indicate the end of the stream and the END_HEADERS flag set to indicate the end of the header section. The CONTINUATION frames, if present, do not have the END_HEADERS flag set. [rfc9113.txt]
records.b_answer: For an HTTP/2 POST that carries request headers and content, the frame sequence consists of a HEADERS frame followed by zero or more CONTINUATION frames. The HEADERS frame has the END_STREAM flag set to indicate that the stream is ending, and the END_HEADERS flag is also set to indicate the end of the header section. The CONTINUATION frames may follow to carry any remaining fragments of the field block. [rfc9113.txt]
